questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: French-speaking and francophile, within Europe, and high-quality healthcare network. The fact that CH has a very private-oriented health sector was a deciding factor, since I wanted to see a different way of running things as opposed to DK, where healthcare is mostly publicly financed.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Nettilac, an agency specialising in short-term rentals, were very accommodating in terms of my needs (3mo., pet-friendly, close to HUG).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: More freedom for sure (I have last lived in a dorm or the sort in 2018), but the pricing is definitely in the adult range. Housing in Geneva on a budget is a fever dream that one wakes up from swiftly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: One prioritises clinical rotations and is placed accordingly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The Exchange Office will do their best to orient exchange students via email to register for their desired rotations; however, I'd prefer if instead of a webpage catalog, a .PDF-borchure with all rotations was made available, as well as up-to-date notes with which rotations are full (
master-.DOCX
, strikeout/delete the pages with the rotations that are not available etc., it can be done easily and will make the whole process more efficient).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Worked out, but got a bit confusing with all the emails.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for specialties you like when choosing your rotations, it shows a lot in the interaction with the doctors, during the OR days etc.; spending time on something you find to be a bore will get old quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations in Plastic Surgery, Medical Genetics, and Clinical Pathology, each with their similarities and particularities.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Every teacher, mentor, doctor were very nice on a personal level, and the attitude was very "you're here to learn" - but much in the stand, watch, and listen way. I wish they'd go easier along with allowing people to engage practically (some already do more than others), but it seemed to be an uphill battle to be more actively involved in the workday. Observing is fine during the first few days, but gets heavy in the long run, especially when days drag on with meetings, conferences, and boards, where the student's cap level is almost always passive listening.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Once again : when choosing rotations opt for specialties you are interested in.

questions.answer: Museums, walks, skiing - depends on interests.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Swiss people are quite easygoing and rarely temperamental, in my experience, so there's room for everyone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that they talk a lot about money.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked being surrounded by mountains, with architectural traits truly at the intersection of Center and West Europe. Also, the average person speaks three languages; my six remained a massive flex still, but I find people are more well-rounded when they have broadened their horizons in such ways that they are fluent in several languages (comes with the territory).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn from people, connect with people, and eat loads of chocolate.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I finally got around to jumping into watercolour as an art medium, it's what I spent my February and March weekends on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The loneliness, but that's part of life. For some of us, at least.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
